items.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: I first worked with him in the early ‘80s in Portland, Oregon. He was in a band I was in.

ctx.x: You got pretty high praise from a drummer that I know that you know very well, and he said that working with you is like having another musician in the band and a co-leader, and that he depends on you a lot because he’s stuck behind the drums, that he communicates through you. And he was telling me about some signals you make that —
That would be Hal Smith I imagine.

items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego and now it’s only two nights a week. But he also works with Marty Grosz and the Orphan Newsboys, and plays jazz parties as a solo. So I’ve got to coordinate that. Rebecca works all the time in Portland

ctx.x: You’ve done quite a bit of band leading. What’s the biggest headache in being a band leader? The biggest thing to surmount?

Coordinating everyone’s schedules. Because nobody can give their loyalty to one band. So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego and now it’s only two nights a week. But he also works with Marty Grosz and the Orphan Newsboys, and plays jazz parties as a solo. So I’ve got to coordinate that. Rebecca works all the time in Portland, freelance and with Dave Frishberg, and she’s on this jazz party circuit. So that’s enough right there. Then the other two guys are…
And now you’re going to be even more spread out, because you’re going to be in New Orleans.
